title: Performing chest compressions during the initial phase of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: continuous vs. alternating – a randomised, prospective mannequin study
summary: At the beginning of resuscitation, many tasks have to be completed simultaneously. This can lead to tasks being interrupted. This could lead to tasks being performed later or less well. The aim is to investigate whether avoiding the regular change of rescuers when performing chest compressions leads to faster completion of important tasks.

interventions.name: Continuous chest compressions without personell change
Alternating chest compressions with personell change

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- informed consent
- completed professional training (Participants who completed the first year of the Notfallsanitäterausbildung can participate as Rettungssanitäter/-in)
Exclusion criteria:
- inability to perform CPR
- study personnel
